assumptions: The TLS connection alone creates Peer from a presented client certificate; HTTP headers cannot create it.
A direct canonical tarball DELETE is classified as an unknown/refused route, never a generic action; a runtime control must confirm zero outbound requests even with a developer bearer.
Certificate admission checks current chain, validity, client-auth purpose, exactly one URI SAN UUID, selected organization root, active member/group and registry on every package request.

Organization-issued admission verifies an issuer-authorized OCSP response matching a fresh nonce and the presented issuer name/key hash plus serial. The issuer responder reflects every committed revocation before acknowledging it; no positive status cache crosses requests.
Every outbound registry/status peer satisfies the per-organization HTTPS, public-routable or operator-approved private host/port/CIDR policy at DNS resolution, connection and redirect hops.
Operation contracts describe future source. Runtime tests must prove exact peer/member/registry values, issuer signature/freshness, response links, clients and no stale-success cache.

Only canonical npm packument GETs carrying a developer token reach serve_token_packument; its selected-upstream token result is authoritative for metadata and does not grant artifact bytes or a later write.

The token-packument operation has no shared-metadata read/write or coalesced result; Slice 3 source review and two-client sequential, concurrent and restart checks must establish this planned contract.

The finite registry-state flows model two same-name registries, a distinct replacement ID after removal, and one old artifact reference. Slice 2 source review and X01/X03 runtime controls must establish exact keys, references, migration, persistence and restart behavior.

Audit outcome selection depends on validating upstream bulk/quick data and current group-visible versions; the finite model checks declared response guarantees, while Slice 3 byte-level tests and independent security review prove input classification, 1,024-lookup bounds and client compatibility.

Version-unpublish lookup is keyed by immutable selected registry, admitted member, npm package, version, filename and digest of the exact upstream-advertised URL; only an atomic, bounded 24-hour encrypted action lease from an admitted `?write=true` preflight can supply it. Runtime tests establish commit, origin/path approval, sealed query, quota, expiry, restart persistence and current principal binding.

A revision PUT parser checks every leased version against its exact selected local link or exact original upstream URL, restores the original for either value, rejects changed URLs before outbound PUT, and preserves ordinary upstream URLs for versions with no lease; N10/N11 runtime tests compare outgoing upstream JSON byte values.

Destination approval is exact registry plus HTTPS origin and segment-boundary path prefix, checked again at DELETE with DNS/connected-peer validation. Credential mode is selected-origin bearer, approved extra-origin bearer, or approved extra-origin anonymous; no redirects. A durable marker from an accepted selected-upstream revision PUT is required for every version DELETE.

Only an accepted selected-upstream revision PUT whose compared prior/current version set removes the exact leased reference may commit a removal marker. A commit failure after acceptance returns uncertain partial write, never success; denied or unchanged PUTs create no marker. Runtime tests prove marker binding and atomic durability.

A successful removal obtains the resulting revision from the selected-upstream PUT response or an immediate authenticated fresh selected-upstream GET that verifies the version absent. Failure to establish it after accepted PUT is uncertain partial write. The marker binds that revision, member and reference, is matched exactly against DELETE, and is consumed once before outbound DELETE; concurrent or replayed DELETE cannot send again.
